###############################################################
# DEFAULT vs TUNED MODEL COMPARISON & SAVE ARTIFACTS
###############################################################

from typing import Dict, Any, Optional
import os
import pandas as pd


def build_tuning_comparison_table(results_df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Construct comparison DataFrame of baseline vs. tuned metrics and compute net delta improvements.

    Parameters
    ----------
    results_df : pd.DataFrame
        DataFrame containing evaluation results for all models.

    Returns
    -------
    pd.DataFrame
        Comparison DataFrame with Accuracy, F1, and ROC-AUC metrics and improvements.
    """
    comparison = pd.DataFrame({
        "Algorithm": [
            "Decision Tree",
            "Random Forest",
            "XGBoost"
        ],

        "Default Accuracy": [
            results_df.loc[results_df.Model == "Decision Tree", "Accuracy"].values[0],
            results_df.loc[results_df.Model == "Random Forest", "Accuracy"].values[0],
            results_df.loc[results_df.Model == "XGBoost", "Accuracy"].values[0]
        ],

        "Tuned Accuracy": [
            results_df.loc[results_df.Model == "Decision Tree (Tuned)", "Accuracy"].values[0],
            results_df.loc[results_df.Model == "Random Forest (Tuned)", "Accuracy"].values[0],
            results_df.loc[results_df.Model == "XGBoost (Tuned)", "Accuracy"].values[0]
        ],

        "Default F1": [
            results_df.loc[results_df.Model == "Decision Tree", "F1"].values[0],
            results_df.loc[results_df.Model == "Random Forest", "F1"].values[0],
            results_df.loc[results_df.Model == "XGBoost", "F1"].values[0]
        ],

        "Tuned F1": [
            results_df.loc[results_df.Model == "Decision Tree (Tuned)", "F1"].values[0],
            results_df.loc[results_df.Model == "Random Forest (Tuned)", "F1"].values[0],
            results_df.loc[results_df.Model == "XGBoost (Tuned)", "F1"].values[0]
        ],

        "Default ROC-AUC": [
            results_df.loc[results_df.Model == "Decision Tree", "ROC_AUC"].values[0],
            results_df.loc[results_df.Model == "Random Forest", "ROC_AUC"].values[0],
            results_df.loc[results_df.Model == "XGBoost", "ROC_AUC"].values[0]
        ],

        "Tuned ROC-AUC": [
            results_df.loc[results_df.Model == "Decision Tree (Tuned)", "ROC_AUC"].values[0],
            results_df.loc[results_df.Model == "Random Forest (Tuned)", "ROC_AUC"].values[0],
            results_df.loc[results_df.Model == "XGBoost (Tuned)", "ROC_AUC"].values[0]
        ]
    })

    comparison["Accuracy Improvement"] = (
        comparison["Tuned Accuracy"] - comparison["Default Accuracy"]
    )

    comparison["F1 Improvement"] = (
        comparison["Tuned F1"] - comparison["Default F1"]
    )

    comparison["ROC Improvement"] = (
        comparison["Tuned ROC-AUC"] - comparison["Default ROC-AUC"]
    )

    try:
        display(comparison.round(3))
    except NameError:
        print(comparison.round(3))

    return comparison


def build_top_features_comparison(
    trained_models: Dict[str, Any],
    feature_names: pd.Index,
    top_n: int = 10
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Generate comparison table of top important features between Random Forest (Tuned) and XGBoost (Tuned).
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("TOP 10 IMPORTANT FEATURES COMPARISON")
    print("=" * 80)

    comparison = pd.DataFrame({
        "Random Forest": trained_models["Random Forest (Tuned)"].feature_importances_,
        "XGBoost": trained_models["XGBoost (Tuned)"].feature_importances_
    }, index=feature_names)

    comparison["Average Importance"] = comparison.mean(axis=1)

    comparison = comparison.sort_values(
        "Average Importance",
        ascending=False
    )

    try:
        display(comparison.head(top_n).round(4))
    except NameError:
        print(comparison.head(top_n).round(4))

    return comparison


def save_research_artifacts(
    results_df: pd.DataFrame,
    comparison: pd.DataFrame,
    feature_importance_dataframes: Optional[Dict[str, pd.DataFrame]] = None,
    base_dir: str = "/content/drive/MyDrive/DataAnalytics_Capstone"
) -> None:
    """
    Export all research outputs: model comparisons, hyperparameter tuning comparison,
    and individual feature importance CSV files.
    """
    os.makedirs(base_dir, exist_ok=True)

    # Save to Excel
    excel_path = f"{base_dir}/Hyperparameter_Tuning_Comparison.xlsx"
    comparison.to_excel(excel_path, index=False)
    print("Hyperparameter tuning comparison saved to Excel.")

    # Save results_df
    results_csv = f"{base_dir}/Model_Comparison.csv"
    results_df.to_csv(results_csv, index=False)
    print("Model comparison saved.")

    # Iterate over the stored feature importance DataFrames
    if feature_importance_dataframes is not None:
        for model_name, importance_df in feature_importance_dataframes.items():
            filename = model_name.replace(" ", "_") + "_Importance.csv"
            importance_df.to_csv(filename, index=False)

    # Also saving hyperparameter comparisons to CSV
    tuning_csv = f"{base_dir}/Hyperparameter_Tuning_Comparison.csv"
    comparison.to_csv(tuning_csv, index=False)

4.2 Target Distribution and Repository EDA

scripts/04_rq2_knowledge_routing_agent/02_target_distribution_and_repository_eda.py

PART-C: RQ2 – Knowledge Routing Agent

1. Inferential Statistics (RQ2 specific)

The dataset contains four repository classes representing the enterprise knowledge required to answer a question. Approximately 46% of questions require Architecture Blueprints and Methodologies in addition to public documentation, followed by Governance (21%) and Pricing (17%). Only 16% of questions can be answered using public documentation alone. This indicates that the majority of enterprise presales questions require internal organizational knowledge beyond publicly available information.

From the above, we note that "Architecture" questions predominantly require Architecture Blueprints and SME expertise, while Governance questions are largely associated with Governance Frameworks and Risk Registers. Commercial questions exhibit stronger associations with Pricing Templates. These initial observations suggest that repository selection is strongly influenced by business context.

"""
# PART-C: RQ2 – Knowledge Routing Agent

## 1. Inferential Statistics (RQ2 specific)

The dataset contains four repository classes representing the enterprise knowledge required to answer a question. Approximately 46% of questions require Architecture Blueprints and Methodologies in addition to public documentation, followed by Governance (21%) and Pricing (17%). Only 16% of questions can be answered using public documentation alone. This indicates that the majority of enterprise presales questions require internal organizational knowledge beyond publicly available information.

From the above, we note that "Architecture" questions predominantly require Architecture Blueprints and SME expertise, while Governance questions are largely associated with Governance Frameworks and Risk Registers. Commercial questions exhibit stronger associations with Pricing Templates. These initial observations suggest that repository selection is strongly influenced by business context.
"""
###############################################################
# RQ2 : TARGET VARIABLE DISTRIBUTION & QUESTION TYPE vs REPOSITORY
###############################################################

from typing import Tuple
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns


def analyze_target_distribution(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Compute count and percentage distribution of Enterprise Knowledge Required and display countplot.

    Parameters
    ----------
    df : pd.DataFrame
        Dataset containing 'Enterprise Knowledge Required'.

    Returns
    -------
    pd.DataFrame
        Distribution DataFrame with Count and Percentage.
    """
    print("=" * 80)
    print("Enterprise Knowledge Repository Distribution")
    print("=" * 80)

    repo_counts = df["Enterprise Knowledge Required"].value_counts()
    repo_percent = round(
        df["Enterprise Knowledge Required"].value_counts(normalize=True) * 100,
        2
    )

    distribution = pd.DataFrame({
        "Count": repo_counts,
        "Percentage": repo_percent
    })

    try:
        display(distribution)
    except NameError:
        print(distribution)

    plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
    sns.countplot(
        data=df,
        y="Enterprise Knowledge Required",
        order=repo_counts.index
    )
    plt.title("Distribution of Enterprise Knowledge Repository")
    plt.xlabel("Number of Questions")
    plt.ylabel("Repository")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

    return distribution


def analyze_question_type_vs_repository(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Generate cross-tabulation and heatmap of Question Type vs Enterprise Knowledge Required.

    Parameters
    ----------
    df : pd.DataFrame
        Dataset containing 'Question Type' and 'Enterprise Knowledge Required'.

    Returns
    -------
    pd.DataFrame
        Cross-tabulation DataFrame.
    """
    cross_tab = pd.crosstab(
        df["Question Type"],
        df["Enterprise Knowledge Required"]
    )

    try:
        display(cross_tab)
    except NameError:
        print(cross_tab)

    plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
    sns.heatmap(
        cross_tab,
        annot=True,
        fmt="d",
        cmap="Blues"
    )
    plt.title("Question Type vs Enterprise Repository")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

    return cross_tab


def run_repository_eda(df: pd.DataFrame) -> Tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """
    Execute full EDA for repository distribution and cross-tabulation.
    """
    dist = analyze_target_distribution(df)
    crosstab = analyze_question_type_vs_repository(df)
    return dist, crosstab

"""
## 1. Inferential Statistics (RQ2 specific) - Chi-square & Cramér's V Analysis

This module performs bivariate Chi-square tests of independence and computes Cramér's V effect sizes
between enterprise presales features and the target repository classes.
"""
###############################################################
# CHI-SQUARE TEST
###############################################################

from typing import List, Optional, Dict, Any
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import chi2_contingency

DEFAULT_TARGET = "Enterprise Knowledge Required"
DEFAULT_FEATURES = [
    "Question Type",
    "Question Intent",
    "Business Capability",
    "Question Complexity"
]


def chi_square_test(feature, target, df=None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Compute Chi-square statistic, p-value, degrees of freedom, and Cramér's V.

    Parameters
    ----------
    feature : str
        Predictor column name.
    target : str
        Target column name.
    df : pd.DataFrame, optional
        Dataset containing the columns.

    Returns
    -------
    Dict[str, Any]
        Dictionary of statistical metrics.
    """
    table = pd.crosstab(
        df[feature],
        df[target]
    )

    chi2, p, dof, expected = chi2_contingency(table)

    n = table.sum().sum()

    k = min(table.shape) - 1

    cramers_v = np.sqrt(
        chi2 / (n * k)
    )

    print("=" * 70)
    print(feature)
    print("=" * 70)
    print("Chi-square :", round(chi2, 2))
    print("p-value :", round(p, 5))
    print("Degrees of Freedom :", dof)
    print("Cramer's V :", round(cramers_v, 3))

    return {
        "Feature": feature,
        "Chi-square": round(chi2, 2),
        "p-value": round(p, 5),
        "Degrees of Freedom": dof,
        "Cramer's V": round(cramers_v, 3)
    }


def run_chi_square_analysis(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    features: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    target: str = DEFAULT_TARGET
) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """
    Iterate over candidate features and run Chi-square tests against target repository.

    Parameters
    ----------
    df : pd.DataFrame
        Dataset to analyze.
    features : Optional[List[str]], optional
        List of candidate features. Defaults to DEFAULT_FEATURES.
    target : str, default=DEFAULT_TARGET
        Target variable name.

    Returns
    -------
    List[Dict[str, Any]]
        List of test results.
    """
    feat_cols = features if features is not None else DEFAULT_FEATURES
    results = []
    for feature in feat_cols:
        res = chi_square_test(feature, target, df=df)
        results.append(res)
    return results

"""
## 2. Feature Engineering

Here, target class is "Enterprise Knowledge Required" with four classes. Lets encode it

###############################################################
# LABEL ENCODING & FEATURE ENGINEERING
###############################################################

from typing import Tuple, List, Optional
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.preprocessing import LabelEncoder

# Updated list of columns to drop for X
DEFAULT_COLUMNS_TO_DROP = [
    "Enterprise Knowledge Required", # Target variable for RQ2
    "Repository_Label",            # Encoded target for RQ2
    "Question",                    # Free text
    "Question_ID",                 # Identifier
    "Source URL",                  # URL string
    "Question URL",                # URL string
    "Official Answer",             # Free text
    "Official Answer Summary",     # Free text
    "Official Documentation URL(s)", # Free text/URL
    "Tags",                        # Free text/high cardinality
    "Notes",                       # Free text
    "Publication Date",            # All NaN
    "Accepted Answer Available?",  # All NaN
    "Accepted Answer URL",         # All NaN
    "Public Knowledge Only?"       # This is the target for RQ1, not a feature for RQ2
]


def encode_target_labels(df: pd.DataFrame) -> Tuple[pd.DataFrame, LabelEncoder]:
    """
    Fit LabelEncoder on 'Enterprise Knowledge Required' and add 'Repository_Label' to df.

    Parameters
    ----------
    df : pd.DataFrame
        Dataset containing 'Enterprise Knowledge Required'.

    Returns
    -------
    Tuple[pd.DataFrame, LabelEncoder]
        Updated DataFrame and fitted LabelEncoder instance.
    """
    encoder = LabelEncoder()
    df["Repository_Label"] = encoder.fit_transform(
        df["Enterprise Knowledge Required"]
    )
    mapping = dict(zip(encoder.classes_, encoder.transform(encoder.classes_)))
    print(mapping)
    return df, encoder


def prepare_features_and_target(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    columns_to_drop: Optional[List[str]] = None
) -> Tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.Series, LabelEncoder, List[str]]:
    """
    Execute feature selection, one-hot encoding, and target encoding.

    Parameters
    ----------
    df : pd.DataFrame
        Cleaned dataset.
    columns_to_drop : Optional[List[str]], optional
        Columns to exclude from predictor matrix.

    Returns
    -------
    Tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.Series, LabelEncoder, List[str]]
        (X, y, encoder, cols_dropped)
    """
    cols_drop = columns_to_drop if columns_to_drop is not None else DEFAULT_COLUMNS_TO_DROP
    df_encoded, encoder = encode_target_labels(df.copy())

    # Create X by dropping the identified problematic columns from a copy of df
    existing_drop_cols = [c for c in cols_drop if c in df_encoded.columns]
    X = df_encoded.drop(columns=existing_drop_cols).copy()

    # Apply one-hot encoding to the remaining categorical columns
    X = pd.get_dummies(X, drop_first=True)

    # Convert any boolean columns (from get_dummies) to integer (0 or 1)
    # This also ensures all columns are numeric (int/float)
    X = X.astype(int)

    y = df_encoded["Repository_Label"]

    print(X.shape)
    print(y.value_counts())

    return X, y, encoder, cols_drop

"""
## 3. Baseline ML models

Let's try different models except Logistic Regression (since the target is multi-class).
This module partitions the dataset into train and test splits (80/20, stratify=y, random_state=42)
and initializes baseline tree-based classifiers: Decision Tree, Random Forest, and XGBoost.
"""
###############################################################
# BUILD BASELINE MODELS (RQ2)
###############################################################

from typing import Tuple, Dict, Any
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.tree import DecisionTreeClassifier
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from xgboost import XGBClassifier


def split_dataset(
    X: pd.DataFrame,
    y: pd.Series,
    test_size: float = 0.2,
    random_state: int = 42
) -> Tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.Series, pd.Series]:
    """
    Split feature matrix X and multiclass target y using stratified sampling.

    Parameters
    ----------
    X : pd.DataFrame
        Design matrix.
    y : pd.Series
        Target vector.
    test_size : float, default=0.2
        Test set fraction.
    random_state : int, default=42
        Seed for reproducibility.

    Returns
    -------
    Tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.Series, pd.Series]
        (X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test)
    """
    X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
        X,
        y,
        test_size=test_size,
        random_state=random_state,
        stratify=y
    )
    return X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test


def build_baseline_models(random_state: int = 42) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Construct baseline multi-class tree models.

    Parameters
    ----------
    random_state : int, default=42
        Seed for reproducibility.

    Returns
    -------
    Dict[str, Any]
        Dictionary of baseline models.
    """
    baseline_models = {
        "Decision Tree":
            DecisionTreeClassifier(
                random_state=random_state
            ),

        "Random Forest":
            RandomForestClassifier(
                random_state=random_state
            ),

        "XGBoost":
            XGBClassifier(
                random_state=random_state,
                eval_metric="mlogloss"
            )
    }
    return baseline_models

"""
## 4. Hyperparameters

This module performs RandomizedSearchCV hyperparameter optimization targeting the f1_macro objective
for multi-class Decision Tree, Random Forest, and XGBoost classifiers.
It preserves the helper function clean_xgb_col_names to sanitize feature names for XGBoost compatibility.
"""
###############################################################
# HYPERPARAMETER TUNING (RQ2)
###############################################################

from typing import Tuple, Any
import re
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import RandomizedSearchCV
from sklearn.tree import DecisionTreeClassifier
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from xgboost import XGBClassifier


def clean_xgb_col_names(df):
    """
    Function to clean column names for XGBoost compatibility.
    Replaces non-alphanumeric characters with underscores and strips edges.
    """
    cols = df.columns
    new_cols = []
    for col in cols:
        # Replace non-alphanumeric characters (excluding underscore) with underscore
        new_col = re.sub('[^A-Za-z0-9_]+', '_', col)
        # Remove leading/trailing underscores if any
        new_col = new_col.strip('_')
        new_cols.append(new_col)
    df.columns = new_cols
    return df


def tune_decision_tree(
    X_train: pd.DataFrame,
    y_train: pd.Series,
    random_state: int = 42
) -> Tuple[Any, RandomizedSearchCV]:
    """
    Tune Decision Tree hyperparameters optimizing f1_macro.
    """
    tree_grid = {
        "criterion": ["gini", "entropy"],
        "max_depth": [3, 5, 7, 10, None],
        "min_samples_split": [2, 5, 10],
        "min_samples_leaf": [1, 2, 4]
    }

    tree_search = RandomizedSearchCV(
        DecisionTreeClassifier(random_state=random_state),
        tree_grid,
        cv=5,
        n_iter=15,
        scoring="f1_macro",
        random_state=random_state,
        n_jobs=-1
    )

    tree_search.fit(X_train, y_train)
    tree_tuned = tree_search.best_estimator_
    print(tree_search.best_params_)
    return tree_tuned, tree_search


def tune_random_forest(
    X_train: pd.DataFrame,
    y_train: pd.Series,
    random_state: int = 42
) -> Tuple[Any, RandomizedSearchCV]:
    """
    Tune Random Forest hyperparameters optimizing f1_macro.
    """
    rf_grid = {
        "n_estimators": [100, 200, 300],
        "max_depth": [5, 10, 15, None],
        "min_samples_leaf": [1, 2, 4],
        "max_features": ["sqrt", "log2"]
    }

    rf_search = RandomizedSearchCV(
        RandomForestClassifier(random_state=random_state),
        rf_grid,
        cv=5,
        n_iter=15,
        scoring="f1_macro",
        random_state=random_state,
        n_jobs=-1
    )

    rf_search.fit(X_train, y_train)
    rf_tuned = rf_search.best_estimator_
    print(rf_search.best_params_)
    return rf_tuned, rf_search


def tune_xgboost(
    X_train: pd.DataFrame,
    y_train: pd.Series,
    random_state: int = 42
) -> Tuple[Any, RandomizedSearchCV]:
    """
    Tune XGBoost hyperparameters optimizing f1_macro.
    """
    xgb_grid = {
        "n_estimators": [100, 200, 300],
        "learning_rate": [0.01, 0.05, 0.1],
        "max_depth": [3, 5, 7],
        "subsample": [0.8, 1],
        "colsample_bytree": [0.8, 1]
    }

    xgb_search = RandomizedSearchCV(
        XGBClassifier(
            random_state=random_state,
            eval_metric="mlogloss"
        ),
        xgb_grid,
        cv=5,
        n_iter=15,
        scoring="f1_macro",
        random_state=random_state,
        n_jobs=-1
    )

    xgb_search.fit(X_train, y_train)
    xgb_tuned = xgb_search.best_estimator_
    print(xgb_search.best_params_)
    return xgb_tuned, xgb_search


def run_all_tuning(
    X_train: pd.DataFrame,
    y_train: pd.Series,
    random_state: int = 42
) -> Tuple[Any, Any, Any]:
    """
    Run full tuning pipeline on sanitized feature matrix.
    """
    X_train_clean = clean_xgb_col_names(X_train.copy())
    tree_tuned, _ = tune_decision_tree(X_train_clean, y_train, random_state)
    rf_tuned, _ = tune_random_forest(X_train_clean, y_train, random_state)
    xgb_tuned, _ = tune_xgboost(X_train_clean, y_train, random_state)
    return tree_tuned, rf_tuned, xgb_tuned

    loader_path = os.path.join(current_dir, "01_environment_and_data_loading.py")

        spec_split.loader.exec_module(mod_split)
        X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = mod_split.split_dataset(X, y)

        tree_tuned, rf_tuned, xgb_tuned = run_all_tuning(X_train, y_train)
        print("Hyperparameter tuning completed.")

"""
## 4. Model Evaluation

This module combines baseline and tuned multi-class models, fits them on sanitized training features,
generates test predictions and predicted class probabilities, and evaluates performance across:
Accuracy, Balanced Accuracy, Precision (macro), Recall (macro), F1 (macro), and ROC_AUC (multiclass OvR macro).
It also generates the detailed classification report and confusion matrix display for the top-performing model.
"""
###############################################################
# COMBINE ALL MODELS, TRAIN ALL MODELS & MODEL EVALUATION
###############################################################

from typing import Dict, Any, Tuple
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from sklearn.metrics import (
    accuracy_score, balanced_accuracy_score, precision_score,
    recall_score, f1_score, roc_auc_score, classification_report,
    ConfusionMatrixDisplay
)


def assemble_all_models(
    baseline_models: Dict[str, Any],
    tree_tuned: Any,
    rf_tuned: Any,
    xgb_tuned: Any
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Combine baseline and tuned models into a single dictionary.
    """
    models = {
        "Decision Tree": baseline_models["Decision Tree"],
        "Decision Tree (Tuned)": tree_tuned,
        "Random Forest": baseline_models["Random Forest"],
        "Random Forest (Tuned)": rf_tuned,
        "XGBoost": baseline_models["XGBoost"],
        "XGBoost (Tuned)": xgb_tuned
    }
    return models


def train_all_models(
    models: Dict[str, Any],
    X_train: pd.DataFrame,
    y_train: pd.Series,
    X_test: pd.DataFrame
) -> Tuple[Dict[str, Any], Dict[str, Any], Dict[str, Any]]:
    """
    Fit each model and compute predictions and probability distributions.
    """
    trained_models = {}
    predictions = {}
    probabilities = {}

    for name, model in models.items():
        print(f"Training {name}")
        model.fit(X_train, y_train)
        trained_models[name] = model
        predictions[name] = model.predict(X_test)
        probabilities[name] = model.predict_proba(X_test)

    return trained_models, predictions, probabilities


def evaluate_models(
    trained_models: Dict[str, Any],
    predictions: Dict[str, Any],
    probabilities: Dict[str, Any],
    y_test: pd.Series
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Calculate comprehensive multiclass evaluation metrics and rank by F1 macro descending.
    """
    results = []

    for name in trained_models:
        pred = predictions[name]
        prob = probabilities[name]

        results.append({
            "Model": name,
            "Accuracy": accuracy_score(y_test, pred),
            "Balanced Accuracy": balanced_accuracy_score(y_test, pred),
            "Precision": precision_score(y_test, pred, average="macro"),
            "Recall": recall_score(y_test, pred, average="macro"),
            "F1": f1_score(y_test, pred, average="macro"),
            "ROC_AUC": roc_auc_score(
                y_test,
                prob,
                multi_class="ovr",
                average="macro"
            )
        })

    results_df = pd.DataFrame(results)
    results_df = results_df.sort_values(
        by="F1",
        ascending=False
    )

    try:
        display(results_df.round(3))
    except NameError:
        print(results_df.round(3))

    return results_df


def report_and_plot_best_model(
    results_df: pd.DataFrame,
    predictions: Dict[str, Any],
    y_test: pd.Series,
    class_names: Any
) -> str:
    """
    Print classification report and display confusion matrix for the top-performing model.
    """
    best_model_name = results_df.iloc[0]["Model"]
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print(f"BEST MODEL : {best_model_name}")
    print("=" * 80)

    print(
        classification_report(
            y_test,
            predictions[best_model_name],
            target_names=class_names
        )
    )

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6))
    ConfusionMatrixDisplay.from_predictions(
        y_test,
        predictions[best_model_name],
        display_labels=class_names,
        cmap="Blues",
        ax=ax
    )
    plt.title(f"Confusion Matrix - {best_model_name}")
    plt.xticks(rotation=25, ha="right")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

    return best_model_name

"""
## 4. Model Evaluation - Stratified Cross Validation

This module executes 5-fold Stratified Cross-Validation on the full feature matrix (sanitized for XGBoost)
evaluating mean Accuracy, Balanced Accuracy, Precision (macro), Recall (macro), and F1 (macro) across all models.
"""
###############################################################
# STEP : STRATIFIED CROSS VALIDATION
###############################################################

from typing import Dict, Any
import re
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import StratifiedKFold, cross_validate


def clean_xgb_col_names(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Function to clean column names for XGBoost compatibility.
    """
    cols = df.columns
    new_cols = []
    for col in cols:
        new_col = re.sub('[^A-Za-z0-9_]+', '_', col)
        new_col = new_col.strip('_')
        new_cols.append(new_col)
    df.columns = new_cols
    return df


def run_stratified_cross_validation(
    trained_models: Dict[str, Any],
    X: pd.DataFrame,
    y: pd.Series,
    n_splits: int = 5,
    random_state: int = 42
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Run 5-fold Stratified Cross-Validation across all trained models.
    """
    X_cleaned = clean_xgb_col_names(X.copy())

    cv = StratifiedKFold(
        n_splits=n_splits,
        shuffle=True,
        random_state=random_state
    )

    metrics = {
        "accuracy": "accuracy",
        "balanced_accuracy": "balanced_accuracy",
        "precision": "precision_macro",
        "recall": "recall_macro",
        "f1": "f1_macro"
    }

    cv_results = []

    for name, model in trained_models.items():
        scores = cross_validate(
            model,
            X_cleaned,
            y,
            cv=cv,
            scoring=metrics,
            n_jobs=-1
        )

        cv_results.append({
            "Model": name,
            "Accuracy": scores["test_accuracy"].mean(),
            "Balanced Accuracy": scores["test_balanced_accuracy"].mean(),
            "Precision": scores["test_precision"].mean(),
            "Recall": scores["test_recall"].mean(),
            "F1": scores["test_f1"].mean()
        })

    cv_df = pd.DataFrame(cv_results)

    try:
        display(cv_df.round(3))
    except NameError:
        print(cv_df.round(3))

    return cv_df

"""
## 4. Model Evaluation - Tuning Comparison & Knowledge Routing Matrix

This module constructs the default vs. tuned F1 improvement comparison table
and computes the empirical Knowledge Routing Matrix (Question Intent vs. Enterprise Knowledge Required, row normalized)
visualized via a seaborn heatmap.
"""
###############################################################
# DEFAULT vs TUNED COMPARISON & KNOWLEDGE ROUTING MATRIX
###############################################################

from typing import Tuple
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns


def build_tuning_comparison(results_df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Compute F1 improvement comparing default and tuned models.
    """
    comparison = []
    pairs = [
        ("Decision Tree", "Decision Tree (Tuned)"),
        ("Random Forest", "Random Forest (Tuned)"),
        ("XGBoost", "XGBoost (Tuned)")
    ]

    for default, tuned in pairs:
        d = results_df[results_df.Model == default].iloc[0]
        t = results_df[results_df.Model == tuned].iloc[0]

        comparison.append({
            "Algorithm": default,
            "Default F1": d["F1"],
            "Tuned F1": t["F1"],
            "Improvement": t["F1"] - d["F1"]
        })

    comparison_df = pd.DataFrame(comparison)

    try:
        display(comparison_df.round(3))
    except NameError:
        print(comparison_df.round(3))

    return comparison_df


def generate_knowledge_routing_matrix(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Generate normalized Knowledge Routing Matrix and render heatmap.
    """
    routing = pd.crosstab(
        df["Question Intent"],
        df["Enterprise Knowledge Required"],
        normalize="index"
    )

    try:
        display(round(routing * 100, 1))
    except NameError:
        print(round(routing * 100, 1))

    plt.figure(figsize=(12, 7))
    sns.heatmap(
        routing,
        annot=True,
        cmap="YlGnBu",
        fmt=".2f"
    )
    plt.title("Knowledge Routing Matrix")
    plt.xlabel("Recommended Repository")
    plt.ylabel("Question Intent")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

    return routing


def run_comparison_and_routing_matrix(
    results_df: pd.DataFrame,
    df: pd.DataFrame
) -> Tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """
    Execute tuning comparison and routing matrix analysis.
    """
    comp_df = build_tuning_comparison(results_df)
    routing_df = generate_knowledge_routing_matrix(df)
    return comp_df, routing_df

"""
## 4. Model Evaluation - Feature Importance Comparison

This module extracts and ranks Gini/entropy feature importances across the three tuned models
(Decision Tree, Random Forest, XGBoost), plots a 3-panel horizontal bar chart of the top 10 features,
and prints formatted top 10 tables for each model.
"""
###############################################################
# STEP : FEATURE IMPORTANCE COMPARISON
###############################################################

from typing import Dict, Any
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt


def extract_and_plot_feature_importances(
    trained_models: Dict[str, Any],
    feature_names: pd.Index,
    top_n: int = 10,
    figsize: tuple = (22, 8)
) -> Dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    """
    Extract feature importances for tuned models, plot 3-panel comparison, and display top features.

    Parameters
    ----------
    trained_models : Dict[str, Any]
        Dictionary of trained model instances.
    feature_names : pd.Index
        Feature column names.
    top_n : int, default=10
        Number of top features to plot and display.
    figsize : tuple, default=(22, 8)
        Plot figure size.

    Returns
    -------
    Dict[str, pd.DataFrame]
        Dictionary mapping model names to sorted feature importance DataFrames.
    """
    models_to_plot = {
        "Decision Tree (Tuned)": trained_models["Decision Tree (Tuned)"],
        "Random Forest (Tuned)": trained_models["Random Forest (Tuned)"],
        "XGBoost (Tuned)": trained_models["XGBoost (Tuned)"]
    }

    feature_importance_tables = {}
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=figsize)

    for ax, (name, model) in zip(axes, models_to_plot.items()):
        importance = pd.DataFrame({
            "Feature": feature_names,
            "Importance": model.feature_importances_
        })

        importance = importance.sort_values(
            by="Importance",
            ascending=False
        )

        feature_importance_tables[name] = importance
        top10 = importance.head(top_n)

        ax.barh(
            top10["Feature"],
            top10["Importance"]
        )
        ax.set_title(name)
        ax.invert_yaxis()

    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

    # Display Top 10 Features
    for name in feature_importance_tables:
        print("\n", "=" * 80)
        print(name)
        print("=" * 80)
        try:
            display(feature_importance_tables[name].head(top_n))
        except NameError:
            print(feature_importance_tables[name].head(top_n))

    return feature_importance_tables

4.11 Routing Demonstration and Handoff Export

scripts/04_rq2_knowledge_routing_agent/11_routing_demonstration_and_handoff_export.py

Save Knowledge Routing Agent

The Knowledge Routing Agent successfully predicts the enterprise knowledge repository required for a given question. Statistical analysis identified significant relationships between question characteristics and repository selection, while machine learning models demonstrated strong predictive capability. Tree-based models consistently identified Question Intent, Business Capability and Question Type as the most influential routing variables. The resulting routing matrix forms the decision logic for the proposed Agentic RAG architecture.

One enhancement for later analysis: My current RQ2 predicts the entire repository combination (e.g., Public Documentation | Architecture Blueprint | Methodology | SME) as a single four-class label. That works, but it doesn't fully reflect how a routing agent behaves.

A more agentic design would treat each repository as an independent decision:

Architecture Blueprint? → Yes/No Methodology? → Yes/No Pricing Template? → Yes/No Governance Framework? → Yes/No SME Consultation? → Yes/No

This becomes a multi-label classification problem rather than a multi-class one. It matches the architecture I described in synopsis much more closely because the agent can route a question to multiple repositories simultaneously instead of choosing only one combined label.

For my interim report, I am keeping the current four-class implementation—it is simpler to explain and demonstrates the concept well. For final dissertation, however, I would consider evolving RQ2 into the multi-label formulation. It would align much better with the design of an actual enterprise Knowledge Routing Agent and strengthen the novelty of my research.

Save the routing model and the objects RQ3 needs to predict repositories for the evaluation questions.

"""
## Save Knowledge Routing Agent

The Knowledge Routing Agent successfully predicts the enterprise knowledge repository required for a given question. Statistical analysis identified significant relationships between question characteristics and repository selection, while machine learning models demonstrated strong predictive capability. Tree-based models consistently identified Question Intent, Business Capability and Question Type as the most influential routing variables. The resulting routing matrix forms the decision logic for the proposed Agentic RAG architecture.

One enhancement for later analysis:
My current RQ2 predicts the entire repository combination (e.g., Public Documentation | Architecture Blueprint | Methodology | SME) as a single four-class label. That works, but it doesn't fully reflect how a routing agent behaves.

A more agentic design would treat each repository as an independent decision:

Architecture Blueprint? → Yes/No
Methodology? → Yes/No
Pricing Template? → Yes/No
Governance Framework? → Yes/No
SME Consultation? → Yes/No

This becomes a multi-label classification problem rather than a multi-class one. It matches the architecture I described in  synopsis much more closely because the agent can route a question to multiple repositories simultaneously instead of choosing only one combined label.

For my interim report, I am keeping the current four-class implementation—it is simpler to explain and demonstrates the concept well. For  final dissertation, however, I would  consider evolving RQ2 into the multi-label formulation. It would align much better with the design of an actual enterprise Knowledge Routing Agent and strengthen the novelty of my research.

Save the routing model and the objects RQ3 needs to predict repositories for the evaluation questions.
"""
###############################################################
# ROUTING DEMONSTRATION, BUSINESS IMPACT & HANDOFF EXPORT
###############################################################

from typing import Dict, Any, List, Tuple
import os
import pickle
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt


def run_routing_demonstration(
    best_model_name: str,
    trained_models: Dict[str, Any],
    X_test: pd.DataFrame,
    y_test: pd.Series,
    encoder: Any
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Demonstrate routing predictions vs ground truth repositories on the test set.
    """
    best_model = trained_models[best_model_name]
    predictions = best_model.predict(X_test)
    predicted_repository = encoder.inverse_transform(predictions)
    actual_repository = encoder.inverse_transform(y_test)

    demo = X_test.copy()
    demo["Actual Repository"] = actual_repository
    demo["Predicted Repository"] = predicted_repository
    demo["Routing Correct"] = np.where(
        demo["Actual Repository"] == demo["Predicted Repository"],
        "Yes",
        "No"
    )

    try:
        display(
            demo[["Actual Repository", "Predicted Repository", "Routing Correct"]].head(20)
        )
    except NameError:
        print(
            demo[["Actual Repository", "Predicted Repository", "Routing Correct"]].head(20)
        )

    return demo


def analyze_business_impact(demo: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Categorize routing impact into correct vs potential misrouting risk.
    """
    impact = demo.copy()
    impact["Business Impact"] = np.where(
        impact["Routing Correct"] == "Yes",
        "Correct repository retrieved",
        "Potential retrieval from incorrect repository"
    )

    try:
        display(
            impact[["Actual Repository", "Predicted Repository", "Routing Correct", "Business Impact"]].head(20)
        )
    except NameError:
        print(
            impact[["Actual Repository", "Predicted Repository", "Routing Correct", "Business Impact"]].head(20)
        )

    return impact


def compute_routing_accuracy_by_repository(impact: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Calculate and plot routing accuracy broken down by repository class.
    """
    routing_accuracy = (
        impact
        .groupby("Actual Repository")["Routing Correct"]
        .apply(lambda x: (x == "Yes").mean() * 100)
        .reset_index()
    )

    routing_accuracy.columns = [
        "Repository",
        "Routing Accuracy (%)"
    ]

    try:
        display(routing_accuracy.round(2))
    except NameError:
        print(routing_accuracy.round(2))

    plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))
    plt.bar(
        routing_accuracy["Repository"],
        routing_accuracy["Routing Accuracy (%)"]
    )
    plt.xticks(rotation=25, ha="right")
    plt.ylabel("Accuracy (%)")
    plt.title("Knowledge Routing Accuracy by Repository")
    plt.grid(axis="y")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

    return routing_accuracy


def generate_routing_decision_table(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Derive the deterministic decision routing table (mode repository per Question Intent).
    """
    routing_table = (
        df.groupby("Question Intent")["Enterprise Knowledge Required"]
        .apply(lambda x: x.value_counts().idxmax())
        .reset_index()
    )

    routing_table.columns = [
        "Question Intent",
        "Recommended Repository"
    ]

    try:
        display(routing_table)
    except NameError:
        print(routing_table)

    return routing_table


def save_rq2_routing_bundle(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    X: pd.DataFrame,
    X_train: pd.DataFrame,
    encoder: Any,
    trained_models: Dict[str, Any],
    best_model_name: str,
    columns_to_drop: List[str],
    handoff_dir: str = "/content/drive/MyDrive/DataAnalytics_Capstone/handoff"
) -> str:
    """
    Persist the complete routing artifacts bundle required by RQ3 for response generation.
    """
    os.makedirs(handoff_dir, exist_ok=True)

    rq2_bundle = {
        "df": df,
        "X": X,
        "X_train": X_train,
        "encoder": encoder,
        "trained_models": trained_models,
        "best_model_name": best_model_name,
        "columns_to_drop": columns_to_drop
    }

    bundle_path = f"{handoff_dir}/rq2_routing_bundle.pkl"
    with open(bundle_path, "wb") as f:
        pickle.dump(rq2_bundle, f)

    print("Knowledge Routing Agent saved.")
    return bundle_path

        results_df = mod_train.evaluate_models(trained_models, predictions, probabilities, y_test)

def clean_xgb_col_names(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Function to clean column names for XGBoost compatibility.
    Replaces non-alphanumeric characters with underscores and strips leading/trailing underscores.
    """
    cols = df.columns
    new_cols = []
    for col in cols:
        new_col = re.sub('[^A-Za-z0-9_]+', '_', col)
        new_col = new_col.strip('_')
        new_cols.append(new_col)
    df.columns = new_cols
    return df


def load_rq2_handoff_bundle(
    base_dir: str = "/content/drive/MyDrive/DataAnalytics_Capstone",
    handoff_subpath: str = "handoff",
    bundle_filename: str = "rq2_routing_bundle.pkl"
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Load the serialized Knowledge Routing Agent bundle from RQ2 handoff directory.

    Parameters
    ----------
    base_dir : str
        Base storage path.
    handoff_subpath : str
        Directory subpath.
    bundle_filename : str

    -------
    Dict[str, Any]

"""
Install the required libraries

Load every repository into LangChain.

Load every PDF and CSV into memory.

Split documents into chunks.
"""
###############################################################
# RQ3 - STEP 3, 4, 5 : DOCUMENT INGESTION & CHUNKING
###############################################################

from typing import Dict, List, Tuple
import os
from langchain_community.document_loaders import PyPDFLoader, CSVLoader
from langchain_text_splitters import RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter
from langchain_core.documents import Document

DEFAULT_BASE_PATH = "/content/enterprise-presales-knowledge-orchestration/data/enterprise_repository"


def define_repositories(base_path: str = DEFAULT_BASE_PATH) -> Dict[str, str]:
    """
    Construct repository folder paths dictionary.
    """
    repositories = {
        "product": os.path.join(base_path, "product"),
        "architecture": os.path.join(base_path, "architecture"),
        "cloud_adoption": os.path.join(base_path, "cloud_adoption"),
        "governance": os.path.join(base_path, "governance"),
        "commercial": os.path.join(base_path, "commercial"),
        "methodology": os.path.join(base_path, "methodology"),
        "operations": os.path.join(base_path, "operations")
    }
    return repositories


def load_documents_from_repositories(
    repositories: Dict[str, str]
) -> List[Document]:
    """
    Load all PDF and CSV files from each repository and tag metadata with repository name.
    """
    documents = []

    for repo_name, folder in repositories.items():
        if not os.path.exists(folder):
            print(f"Warning: Folder {folder} not found. Skipping.")
            continue

        print(f"\nLoading {repo_name}")
        for file in os.listdir(folder):
            path = os.path.join(folder, file)
            if file.endswith(".pdf"):
                loader = PyPDFLoader(path)
                docs = loader.load()
            elif file.endswith(".csv"):
                loader = CSVLoader(path)
                docs = loader.load()
            else:
                continue

            for d in docs:
                d.metadata["repository"] = repo_name

            documents.extend(docs)

    print("Total documents:", len(documents))
    return documents


def chunk_documents(
    documents: List[Document],
    chunk_size: int = 1000,
    chunk_overlap: int = 200
) -> List[Document]:
    """
    Split documents into chunks using RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter.
    """
    splitter = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter(
        chunk_size=chunk_size,
        chunk_overlap=chunk_overlap
    )
    chunks = splitter.split_documents(documents)
    print("Chunks created:", len(chunks))
    return chunks


def run_ingestion_and_chunking(
    base_path: str = DEFAULT_BASE_PATH,
    chunk_size: int = 1000,
    chunk_overlap: int = 200
) -> Tuple[List[Document], List[Document]]:
    """
    Execute full ingestion and chunking pipeline.
    """
    repos = define_repositories(base_path)
    documents = load_documents_from_repositories(repos)
    chunks = chunk_documents(documents, chunk_size, chunk_overlap)
    return documents, chunks


if __name__ == "__main__":
    docs, chunks = run_ingestion_and_chunking()

Build the vector database, with  one vector database for each enterprise knowledge repository.

###############################################################
# RQ3 - STEP 6, 7, 8 : EMBEDDINGS & VECTOR DATABASES
###############################################################

from typing import List, Dict, Any, Tuple
from collections import defaultdict
import os
import pandas as pd
from langchain_core.documents import Document
from langchain_chroma import Chroma
from langchain_openai import OpenAIEmbeddings


def initialize_embedding_model(
    model_name: str = "text-embedding-3-small"
) -> OpenAIEmbeddings:
    """
    Initialize OpenAI embeddings model using OPENAI_API_KEY from environment or Colab userdata.
    """
    try:
        from google.colab import userdata
        api_key = userdata.get('OPENAI_API_KEY')
        if api_key:
            os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"] = api_key
    except ImportError:
        pass

    embedding_model = OpenAIEmbeddings(
        model=model_name
    )
    return embedding_model


def build_repository_vector_databases(
    chunks: List[Document],
    embedding_model: OpenAIEmbeddings,
    base_persist_dir: str = "./vectordb"
) -> Dict[str, Chroma]:
    """
    Create one Chroma vector database for each knowledge repository.

    Parameters
    ----------
    chunks : List[Document]
        Document chunks tagged with repository metadata.
    embedding_model : OpenAIEmbeddings
        Initialized embedding model.
    base_persist_dir : str
        Directory to persist Chroma databases.

    Returns
    -------
    Dict[str, Chroma]
        Dictionary mapping repository names to Chroma database instances.
    """
    vector_dbs = {}

    # Group chunks by repository
    repository_chunks = defaultdict(list)
    for chunk in chunks:
        repository = chunk.metadata["repository"]
        repository_chunks[repository].append(chunk)

    print("=" * 80)
    print("Building Repository Vector Databases")
    print("=" * 80)

    for repository, docs in repository_chunks.items():
        persist_dir = f"{base_persist_dir}/{repository}"

        db = Chroma.from_documents(
            documents=docs,
            embedding=embedding_model,
            persist_directory=persist_dir
        )

        vector_dbs[repository] = db
        print(f"{repository:20s} -> {len(docs):5d} chunks")

    print("\nVector databases created successfully.")
    return vector_dbs


def verify_vector_databases(vector_dbs: Dict[str, Chroma]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Verify indexed chunk count per repository vector database.
    """
    print("=" * 80)
    print("Repository Summary")
    print("=" * 80)

    summary = []
    for repo in vector_dbs:
        count = vector_dbs[repo]._collection.count()
        summary.append([repo, count])

    summary_df = pd.DataFrame(
        summary,
        columns=["Repository", "Indexed Chunks"]
    )

    try:
        display(summary_df)
    except NameError:
        print(summary_df)

    return summary_df


def run_vector_db_pipeline(
    chunks: List[Document],
    base_persist_dir: str = "./vectordb"
) -> Tuple[Dict[str, Chroma], pd.DataFrame]:
    """
    Execute full embeddings and vector database construction pipeline.
    """
    embed_model = initialize_embedding_model()
    vector_dbs = build_repository_vector_databases(chunks, embed_model, base_persist_dir)
    summary_df = verify_vector_databases(vector_dbs)
    return vector_dbs, summary_df


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import importlib.util

    current_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    ingest_path = os.path.join(current_dir, "03_document_ingestion_and_chunking.py")

    if os.path.exists(ingest_path):
        spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("step_03_ingest", ingest_path)
        mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
        spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
        _, chunks = mod.run_ingestion_and_chunking()
        vector_dbs, summary_df = run_vector_db_pipeline(chunks)

"""
Retrieve only from the repository selected by RQ2.

Verify that the routing mechanism retrieves relevant information from the repository.

This section retrieves knowledge only from the repositories identified by the Knowledge Routing Agent (RQ2).
"""
###############################################################
# RQ3 - STEP 9, 10, 11 : SINGLE & MULTI-REPOSITORY RETRIEVAL
###############################################################

from typing import Dict, List, Tuple, Any, Optional

DEFAULT_REPOSITORY_MAPPING = {
    "public documentation": "product",
    "architecture blueprint": "architecture",
    "methodology": "methodology",
    "governance framework": "governance",
    "commercial model": "commercial",
    "pricing template": "commercial",
    "operations": "operations",
    "cloud adoption": "cloud_adoption",
    "risk register": "governance",
    "sme": "product"
}


def retrieve_context(
    question: str,
    repository: str,
    top_k: int = 5,
    vector_dbs: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None
) -> str:
    """
    Retrieve relevant chunks from the selected single repository.
    """
    db = vector_dbs[repository]

    retriever = db.as_retriever(
        search_kwargs={"k": top_k}
    )

    docs = retriever.invoke(question)

    context = "\n\n".join(
        [d.page_content for d in docs]
    )

    return context


def test_single_retrieval(
    question: str,
    repository_full_string: str,
    vector_dbs: Dict[str, Any],
    mapping: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None
) -> str:
    """
    Test retrieval from the first component of the required repository string.
    """
    repo_map = mapping if mapping is not None else DEFAULT_REPOSITORY_MAPPING
    first_repo_component_raw = repository_full_string.split("|")[0].strip().lower()
    repository = repo_map.get(first_repo_component_raw, "product")

    print("=" * 80)
    print("Question")
    print("=" * 80)
    print(question)
    print("\nRepository (for single-repo test)")
    print(repository)
    print("\nRetrieved Context")

    context = retrieve_context(question, repository, top_k=5, vector_dbs=vector_dbs)
    print(context[:3000])
    return context


def retrieve_multi_repository_context(
    question: str,
    repositories: List[str],
    top_k: int = 3,
    vector_dbs: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None
) -> Tuple[str, List[Dict[str, str]]]:
    """
    Retrieve knowledge from one or more repositories selected by Knowledge Routing Agent (RQ2).
    """
    all_context = []
    retrieved_sources = []

    mapping = DEFAULT_REPOSITORY_MAPPING

    for repo in repositories:
        repo = repo.strip().lower()

        if repo not in mapping:
            continue

        repo_name = mapping[repo]

        if repo_name not in vector_dbs:
            continue

        retriever = vector_dbs[repo_name].as_retriever(
            search_kwargs={"k": top_k}
        )

        docs = retriever.invoke(question)

        for d in docs:
            all_context.append(d.page_content)
            retrieved_sources.append({
                "Repository": repo_name,
                "Source": d.metadata.get("source", "Unknown")
            })

    context = "\n\n".join(all_context)
    return context, retrieved_sources


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("Context retrieval mechanisms defined.")

Question: What is CloudWatch Container Insights?
Official Answer: CloudWatch Container Insights collects, aggregates, and summarizes metrics and logs from your containerized applications and microservices running on Amazon ECS, Amazon EKS, Kubernetes platforms on Amazon EC2, and AWS Fargate (for both Amazon ECS and Amazon EKS). Container Insights collects container metrics such as CPU, memory, disk, and network metrics out of the box and provides deeper diagnostic information, such as container restart failures, to help you isolate issues and resolve them quickly. Container Insights delivers your container observability in automatic dashboards enabling you to monitor your application health and performance easily. Container Insights also supports collecting EKS metrics via OTLP, with PromQL query support and up to 150 labels per metric. You can also set CloudWatch alarms on Container Insights metrics to be notified of anomalies before your application performance is impacted.

It provides container-level visibility — CPU, memory, disk, network, and GPU metrics across clusters, nodes, pods, and containers — using the OpenTelemetry standard for collection and transport. You can query these metrics using PromQL, set alarms, and visualize them in automatic dashboards. Because it uses open-source receivers and the OpenTelemetry format, you can send data to CloudWatch and third-party destinations from the same collection pipeline without proprietary agents. """
Generate enterprise responses using the retrieved multi-repository knowledge.

Validate that repository routing, retrieval and response generation are functioning correctly.

Store generated enterprise responses for reproducibility and to avoid regenerating during iterative analysis.

Baseline GPT (No Enterprise Knowledge): Generate responses using only GPT internal knowledge.

Agentic RAG (Ground Truth Repository): Generate responses using the actual repositories annotated in the corpus.

Agentic RAG (RQ2 Predicted Repository): Use the repository predicted by the Knowledge Routing Agent.

Agentic RAG (All Repositories) - Retrieve from every repository without routing.
"""
###############################################################
# RQ3 - STEP 12 TO 18 : RESPONSE GENERATION AGENT & 4 STRATEGIES
###############################################################

from typing import Dict, Any, Optional
import os
import time
from openai import OpenAI

DEFAULT_MODEL = "gpt-4.1"


def get_openai_client() -> OpenAI:
    """
    Instantiate OpenAI client from environment variable.
    """
    return OpenAI(api_key=os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"])


def generate_enterprise_response(
    question: str,
    retrieved_context: str,
    client: Optional[OpenAI] = None,
    model: str = DEFAULT_MODEL
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Generate structured enterprise response using retrieved knowledge.
    """
    cli = client if client is not None else get_openai_client()

    prompt = f"""

You are a Senior Enterprise Presales Architect.

Answer the question using ONLY the retrieved enterprise knowledge.

If information is unavailable,
say so.

Question

{question}

Enterprise Knowledge

{retrieved_context}

Generate

1. Executive Summary

2. Technical Explanation

3. Architecture or Implementation Recommendations

4. Presales Positioning or Client Advice

"""

    response = cli.chat.completions.create(
        model=model,
        messages=[
            {
                "role": "system",
                "content": "You are an enterprise AI assistant."
            },
            {
                "role": "user",
                "content": prompt
            }
        ],
        temperature=0.2
    )

    return {
        "response": response.choices[0].message.content,
        "prompt": prompt,
        "model": model
    }


def baseline_response(
    question: str,
    client: Optional[OpenAI] = None,
    model: str = DEFAULT_MODEL
) -> str:
    """
    Strategy 1: Generate response using only GPT internal knowledge without enterprise context.
    """
    cli = client if client is not None else get_openai_client()

    response = cli.chat.completions.create(
        model=model,
        messages=[
            {
                "role": "system",
                "content": "You are a helpful enterprise presales architect. Answer the question directly."
            },
            {
                "role": "user",
                "content": question
            }
        ],
        temperature=0.2
    )
    return response.choices[0].message.content


def ground_truth_rag(
    question: str,
    required_repo: str,
    vector_dbs: Dict[str, Any],
    client: Optional[OpenAI] = None,
    retrieve_fn=None
) -> str:
    """
    Strategy 2: Retrieve from ground truth repository and generate response.
    """
    repos = required_repo.split("|")
    context, sources = retrieve_fn(question, repos, vector_dbs=vector_dbs)
    result = generate_enterprise_response(question, context, client=client)
    return result["response"]


def predicted_rag(
    question: str,
    predicted_repo: str,
    vector_dbs: Dict[str, Any],
    client: Optional[OpenAI] = None,
    retrieve_fn=None
) -> str:
    """
    Strategy 3: Retrieve from RQ2 predicted repository and generate response.
    """
    repos = predicted_repo.split("|")
    context, sources = retrieve_fn(question, repos, vector_dbs=vector_dbs)
    result = generate_enterprise_response(question, context, client=client)
    return result["response"]


def all_repository_rag(
    question: str,
    vector_dbs: Dict[str, Any],
    client: Optional[OpenAI] = None,
    retrieve_fn=None
) -> str:
    """
    Strategy 4: Retrieve from all repositories without routing and generate response.
    """
    all_repos = list(vector_dbs.keys())
    context, sources = retrieve_fn(question, all_repos, vector_dbs=vector_dbs)
    result = generate_enterprise_response(question, context, client=client)
    return result["response"]


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("Response generation strategies defined.")

1. Executive Summary  
CloudWatch Container Insights is an AWS monitoring solution that provides comprehensive visibility into the performance and health of containerized applications running on Amazon ECS, Amazon EKS, Kubernetes (on EC2), and AWS Fargate. By automating the collection, aggregation, and summarization of metrics and logs, it enables organizations to proactively monitor and quickly respond to performance or reliability issues in their microservices environments.

2. Technical Explanation  
CloudWatch Container Insights automatically collects and analyzes metrics like CPU, memory, disk, and network usage from your containers. It also gathers diagnostic information such as container restart failures. This data is presented in out-of-the-box dashboards that summarize the health and performance of your containerized workloads. In addition, enhanced metrics collection is supported for EKS via OTLP, including PromQL query support and up to 150 labels per metric. CloudWatch alarms can be set on these metrics to notify teams of abnormal behavior before it impacts application performance. Metrics and logs can be further queried or aggregated for custom reports and alerting.

3. Enterprise Recommendation  
Enterprises running containerized workloads on AWS should enable CloudWatch Container Insights to achieve centralized, automated observability. This increases operational agility, speeds incident response, and supports compliance by maintaining a detailed operational record. Container Insights is particularly valuable for organizations adopting microservices architectures at scale, as it reduces monitoring complexity and highlights actionable information via automated dashboards and alerting.

4. Risks  
- Overreliance on default dashboards may obscure unique workload problems unless custom metrics and alerts are configured.
- Potential for increased AWS costs due to metrics and log ingestion, especially in large-scale environments.
- Delayed detection of complex cross-system issues if logs and metrics are not integrated with broader enterprise monitoring tools.

5. Best Practices  
- Regularly review and customize CloudWatch Container Insights dashboards to reflect key business and technical metrics.
- Set up targeted CloudWatch alarms on critical metrics (such as error rates, restart counts, resource saturation).
- Utilize OTLP and PromQL features for granular EKS monitoring.
- Integrate Container Insights data with incident management workflows to accelerate response.
- Periodically review log and metric retention policies to optimize costs and compliance.

"""

Save Results:

###############################################################
# RQ3 - STEP 19 & 20 : EXPERIMENT RUNNER & RESULTS PERSISTENCE
###############################################################

from typing import Dict, Any, Optional
import os
import io
import pandas as pd
from xgboost import XGBClassifier


def align_and_predict_repositories(
    evaluation_df: pd.DataFrame,
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    X: pd.DataFrame,
    X_train: pd.DataFrame,
    trained_models: Dict[str, Any],
    best_model_name: str,
    encoder: Any,
    clean_xgb_fn=None
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Generate RQ2 predicted repository labels for all questions in evaluation_df.
    """
    eval_df = evaluation_df.copy()

    # 1. Get Question_IDs from evaluation_df
    evaluation_question_ids = eval_df['Question_ID'].tolist()

    # 2. Filter original X using matching Question_IDs
    original_df_indices_for_evaluation = df[df['Question_ID'].isin(evaluation_question_ids)].index
    X_evaluation_features = X.loc[original_df_indices_for_evaluation].copy()

    # 3. Apply column cleaning if XGBoost model
    best_model = trained_models[best_model_name]
    if clean_xgb_fn is not None and isinstance(best_model, (type(XGBClassifier()), type(XGBClassifier(random_state=42, eval_metric="mlogloss")))):
        X_evaluation_features = clean_xgb_fn(X_evaluation_features)

    # 4. Reindex X_evaluation_features to match X_train columns
    trained_columns = X_train.columns
    X_evaluation_features = X_evaluation_features.reindex(columns=trained_columns, fill_value=0)

    # 5. Predict repositories
    predicted_labels = best_model.predict(X_evaluation_features)

    # 6. Inverse transform
    predicted_repositories_names = encoder.inverse_transform(predicted_labels)

    # 7. Add 'Predicted Repository' column
    predicted_series = pd.Series(predicted_repositories_names, index=eval_df.index)
    eval_df['Predicted Repository'] = predicted_series

    return eval_df


def run_rq3_experiments(
    evaluation_df: pd.DataFrame,
    vector_dbs: Dict[str, Any],
    baseline_fn,
    ground_truth_fn,
    predicted_fn,
    all_repo_fn,
    retrieve_fn,
    sample_n: int = 100
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Execute all 4 response generation strategies across evaluation questions.
    """
    experiment_results = []
    subset_df = evaluation_df.head(sample_n)
    N = len(subset_df)

    for idx, row in subset_df.iterrows():
        question = row["Question"]
        print(f"Running Question {idx+1}/{N}")

        baseline = baseline_fn(question)

        gt = ground_truth_fn(
            question,
            row["Enterprise Knowledge Required"],
            vector_dbs=vector_dbs,
            retrieve_fn=retrieve_fn
        )

        predicted = predicted_fn(
            question,
            row["Predicted Repository"],
            vector_dbs=vector_dbs,
            retrieve_fn=retrieve_fn
        )

        all_repo = all_repo_fn(
            question,
            vector_dbs=vector_dbs,
            retrieve_fn=retrieve_fn
        )

        experiment_results.append({
            "Question": question,
            "Reference": row.get("Official Answer", row.get("Answer", "")),
            "Baseline": baseline,
            "GroundTruth": gt,
            "Predicted": predicted,
            "AllRepositories": all_repo
        })

    experiment_df = pd.DataFrame(experiment_results)

    try:
        display(experiment_df.head())
    except NameError:
        print(experiment_df.head())

    return experiment_df


def save_experiment_results(
    experiment_df: pd.DataFrame,
    output_path: str = "/content/drive/MyDrive/DataAnalytics_Capstone/rq3_generation_results.csv"
) -> str:
    """
    Save generation experiment results to CSV.
    """
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(output_path), exist_ok=True)
    csv_string = experiment_df.to_csv(index=False)
    with open(output_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(csv_string)
    print("Results saved.")
    return output_path


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("Experiment runner and results persistence module ready.")

"""
LLM-as-a-Judge: Each response will be scored on:
- accuracy
- completeness
- enterprise_relevance
- technical_correctness
- actionability
- overall

Response Quality Index (RQI): This gives us a single metric for comparing responses across strategies.
"""
###############################################################
# RQ3 - STEP 21, 22, 23 : LLM-AS-A-JUDGE & RQI CALCULATION
###############################################################

from typing import Dict, Any, Optional
import os
import re
import json
import time
import pandas as pd
from openai import OpenAI

DEFAULT_MODEL = "gpt-4.1"


def evaluate_response(
    question: str,
    reference: str,
    generated: str,
    client: Optional[OpenAI] = None,
    model: str = DEFAULT_MODEL
) -> str:
    """
    Evaluate generated response against reference using LLM-as-a-Judge returning structured JSON scores.
    """
    cli = client if client is not None else OpenAI(api_key=os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"])

    prompt = f"""
You are an expert evaluator of enterprise presales responses.

Question:
{question}

Reference Answer:
{reference}

Generated Answer:
{generated}

Evaluate the generated answer against the reference.

Return ONLY JSON.

{{
"accuracy":0,
"completeness":0,
"enterprise_relevance":0,
"technical_correctness":0,
"actionability":0,
"overall":0
}}
"""
    # Uses responses.create (or chat.completions fallback) matching notebook implementation
    try:
        response = cli.responses.create(
            model=model,
            input=prompt
        )
        return response.output_text
    except AttributeError:
        response = cli.chat.completions.create(
            model=model,
            messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
            temperature=0.0
        )
        return response.choices[0].message.content


def calculate_rqi(
    accuracy: float,
    completeness: float,
    enterprise_relevance: float,
    technical_correctness: float,
    actionability: float
) -> float:
    """
    Calculate the composite Response Quality Index (RQI) as the unweighted mean of all 5 dimensions.
    """
    return (
        accuracy +
        completeness +
        enterprise_relevance +
        technical_correctness +
        actionability
    ) / 5


def parse_llm_json_output_robustly(json_string_candidate: Any) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Helper function to parse LLM JSON output robustly, stripping markdown fences and trailing tokens.
    """
    if not isinstance(json_string_candidate, str):
        return {"overall": 0, "accuracy": 0, "completeness": 0, "enterprise_relevance": 0, "technical_correctness": 0, "actionability": 0}

    cleaned_string = json_string_candidate.strip()
    cleaned_string = re.sub(r'^```json\s*|\s*```$', '', cleaned_string, flags=re.DOTALL).strip()

    try:
        return json.loads(cleaned_string)
    except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
        if "Extra data" in str(e) and e.pos is not None:
            try:
                return json.loads(cleaned_string[:e.pos])
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                pass
        print(f"Warning: Failed to parse LLM JSON output. Returning default scores. Error: {e}.")
        return {"overall": 0, "accuracy": 0, "completeness": 0, "enterprise_relevance": 0, "technical_correctness": 0, "actionability": 0}
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Warning: Unexpected error during JSON parsing: {e}.")
        return {"overall": 0, "accuracy": 0, "completeness": 0, "enterprise_relevance": 0, "technical_correctness": 0, "actionability": 0}


def run_llm_judge(
    experiment_df: pd.DataFrame,
    client: Optional[OpenAI] = None,
    model: str = DEFAULT_MODEL
) -> Tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """
    Execute LLM Judge across all strategies and parse evaluation scores into analysis_df.
    """
    print("Running LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation...")
    judge_start_time = time.time()

    exp_df = experiment_df.copy()
    exp_df["Baseline_Judge"] = ""
    exp_df["GroundTruth_Judge"] = ""
    exp_df["Predicted_Judge"] = ""
    exp_df["AllRepositories_Judge"] = ""

    for idx, row in exp_df.iterrows():
        question = row["Question"]
        reference = row["Reference"]

        exp_df.at[idx, "Baseline_Judge"] = evaluate_response(question, reference, row["Baseline"], client, model)
        exp_df.at[idx, "GroundTruth_Judge"] = evaluate_response(question, reference, row["GroundTruth"], client, model)
        exp_df.at[idx, "Predicted_Judge"] = evaluate_response(question, reference, row["Predicted"], client, model)
        exp_df.at[idx, "AllRepositories_Judge"] = evaluate_response(question, reference, row["AllRepositories"], client, model)

    judge_end_time = time.time()
    print(f"LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation completed in {round(judge_end_time - judge_start_time, 2)} seconds.")

    # Prepare analysis dataset
    score_rows = []
    for _, row in exp_df.iterrows():
        b_scores = parse_llm_json_output_robustly(row["Baseline_Judge"])
        gt_scores = parse_llm_json_output_robustly(row["GroundTruth_Judge"])
        p_scores = parse_llm_json_output_robustly(row["Predicted_Judge"])
        all_scores = parse_llm_json_output_robustly(row["AllRepositories_Judge"])

        score_rows.append({
            "Question": row["Question"],
            "Baseline": b_scores.get("overall", calculate_rqi(b_scores.get("accuracy", 0), b_scores.get("completeness", 0), b_scores.get("enterprise_relevance", 0), b_scores.get("technical_correctness", 0), b_scores.get("actionability", 0))),
            "GroundTruth": gt_scores.get("overall", calculate_rqi(gt_scores.get("accuracy", 0), gt_scores.get("completeness", 0), gt_scores.get("enterprise_relevance", 0), gt_scores.get("technical_correctness", 0), gt_scores.get("actionability", 0))),
            "Predicted": p_scores.get("overall", calculate_rqi(p_scores.get("accuracy", 0), p_scores.get("completeness", 0), p_scores.get("enterprise_relevance", 0), p_scores.get("technical_correctness", 0), p_scores.get("actionability", 0))),
            "AllRepositories": all_scores.get("overall", calculate_rqi(all_scores.get("accuracy", 0), all_scores.get("completeness", 0), all_scores.get("enterprise_relevance", 0), all_scores.get("technical_correctness", 0), all_scores.get("actionability", 0)))
        })

    analysis_df = pd.DataFrame(score_rows)
    return exp_df, analysis_df


def save_analysis_dataset(
    analysis_df: pd.DataFrame,
    output_path: str = "/content/drive/MyDrive/DataAnalytics_Capstone/rq3_analysis_df"
) -> str:
    """
    Persist analysis DataFrame to CSV.
    """
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(output_path), exist_ok=True)
    csv_string = analysis_df.to_csv(index=False)
    with open(output_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(csv_string)
    print("Analysis saved.")
    return output_path

"""
Descriptive Statistics: Summarize the performance of each response generation strategy using mean, standard deviation, median and interquartile range (IQR).

Boxplot: Compare the distribution of Response Quality Index (RQI) across the four response generation systems.

Assumption Testing - Determine whether parametric statistical tests are appropriate:
1. Normality Test (Shapiro-Wilk)
"""
###############################################################
# RQ3 - STEP 24, 25, 26 : DESCRIPTIVE STATISTICS, BOXPLOT & NORMALITY
###############################################################

from typing import List, Optional
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.stats import shapiro

DEFAULT_SCORE_COLUMNS = ['Baseline', 'GroundTruth', 'Predicted', 'AllRepositories']


def compute_descriptive_statistics(
    analysis_df: pd.DataFrame,
    score_columns: Optional[List[str]] = None
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Generate descriptive statistics summary with Mean, Std, Median, and IQR.
    """
    cols = score_columns if score_columns is not None else DEFAULT_SCORE_COLUMNS
    summary = analysis_df[cols].describe().T

    summary["Median"] = analysis_df[cols].median()
    summary["IQR"] = (
        analysis_df[cols].quantile(0.75) - analysis_df[cols].quantile(0.25)
    )

    try:
        display(summary)
    except NameError:
        print(summary)

    return summary


def plot_rqi_boxplot(
    analysis_df: pd.DataFrame,
    score_columns: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    figsize: tuple = (9, 6)
) -> None:
    """
    Render boxplot comparing the distribution of Response Quality Index (RQI) across systems.
    """
    cols = score_columns if score_columns is not None else DEFAULT_SCORE_COLUMNS
    plt.figure(figsize=figsize)
    analysis_df[cols].boxplot()
    plt.ylabel("Response Quality Index")
    plt.title("Comparison of Response Quality")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()


def test_normality_assumptions(
    analysis_df: pd.DataFrame,
    score_columns: Optional[List[str]] = None
) -> dict:
    """
    Perform Shapiro-Wilk test of normality across all response generation strategies.
    """
    cols = score_columns if score_columns is not None else DEFAULT_SCORE_COLUMNS
    results = {}

    for col in cols:
        stat, p = shapiro(analysis_df[col])
        print("=" * 60)
        print(col)
        print("Statistic:", round(stat, 3))
        print("p-value:", round(p, 4))
        if p > 0.05:
            conclusion = "Normally Distributed"
        else:
            conclusion = "Not Normally Distributed"
        print(conclusion)

        results[col] = {
            "Statistic": round(stat, 3),
            "p-value": round(p, 4),
            "Conclusion": conclusion
        }

    return results


def run_descriptive_and_normality_checks(analysis_df: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple:
    """
    Execute full descriptive statistics and normality assumption test suite.
    """
    summary = compute_descriptive_statistics(analysis_df)
    plot_rqi_boxplot(analysis_df)
    normality = test_normality_assumptions(analysis_df)
    return summary, normality


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("Descriptive statistics and normality module ready.")

"""
Repeated Measures ANOVA: Compare mean response quality across the four response generation strategies.

Friedman Test: Non-parametric comparison of the four response generation strategies.
"""
###############################################################
# RQ3 - STEP 27 & 28 : REPEATED MEASURES ANOVA & FRIEDMAN TEST
###############################################################

from typing import Tuple, Any
import pandas as pd
from statsmodels.stats.anova import AnovaRM
from scipy.stats import friedmanchisquare


def run_repeated_measures_anova(analysis_df: pd.DataFrame) -> Any:
    """
    Perform Repeated Measures ANOVA across methods using Question as subject.

    Parameters
    ----------
    analysis_df : pd.DataFrame
        DataFrame with Question and the 4 method columns.

    Returns
    -------
    Any
        Fitted AnovaRM results.
    """
    print("=" * 80)
    print("REPEATED MEASURES ANOVA")
    print("=" * 80)

    anova_df = analysis_df.melt(
        id_vars="Question",
        var_name="Method",
        value_name="RQI"
    )

    anova = AnovaRM(
        anova_df,
        depvar="RQI",
        subject="Question",
        within=["Method"]
    )

    results = anova.fit()
    print(results)
    return results


def run_friedman_test(analysis_df: pd.DataFrame) -> Tuple[float, float]:
    """
    Perform non-parametric Friedman test across the four response generation strategies.

    Returns
    -------
    Tuple[float, float]
        (Chi-square statistic, p-value)
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("FRIEDMAN TEST (NON-PARAMETRIC)")
    print("=" * 80)

    stat, p = friedmanchisquare(
        analysis_df["Baseline"],
        analysis_df["GroundTruth"],
        analysis_df["Predicted"],
        analysis_df["AllRepositories"]
    )

    print("Statistic:", stat)
    print("p-value:", p)
    return stat, p


def run_hypothesis_tests(analysis_df: pd.DataFrame) -> Tuple[Any, Tuple[float, float]]:
    """
    Execute both parametric (ANOVA) and non-parametric (Friedman) omni-bus hypothesis tests.
    """
    anova_res = run_repeated_measures_anova(analysis_df)
    friedman_res = run_friedman_test(analysis_df)
    return anova_res, friedman_res

    print("Repeated Measures ANOVA and Friedman test module ready.")
